title: Etale invariant spectra for cartesian stabilizer-preserving affine groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $F:(U',R',s',t',e',i',c')\to(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a morphism of groupoid schemes over $S$, meaning maps $a:U'\to U$ and $b:R'\to R$ commuting with all operations of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Assume $U,R,U',R'$ are affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], all four source and target maps are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and $a$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $G=R\times_{(s,t),U\times_SU,\Delta_U}U$ and $G'=R'\times_{(s',t'),U'\times_SU',\Delta_{U'}}U'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume the three natural squares with horizontal maps $b,a$, and respectively vertical maps $(s',s)$, $(t',t)$, and $(G'\to U',G\to U)$, are cartesian; in the last square the upper horizontal map is $G'\to G$. Define $C=\{f\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U):s^*f=t^*f\}$ and $C'=\{f\in\Gamma(U',\mathcal O_{U'}):(s')^*f=(t')^*f\}$. Then the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale, and the natural map $U'\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}C'$ is an isomorphism. Empty schemes and variable finite locally free ranks are allowed.

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and similarly with primes, and put $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $M\prime=\operatorname{Spec}C\prime$. The operations commute with the maps to $M$, since $s^*c=t^*c$ for $c\in C$. For any flat $C$-algebra $D$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to $0\to C\to A\xrightarrow{s^*-t^*}B$. It identifies the invariants in $A\otimes_C D$ with $D$. Applied instead to $0\to C\prime\to A\prime\to B\prime$ over $C$, it identifies the primed invariants with $C\prime\otimes_C D$. Thus the two invariant spectra after flat base change really are $\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $M\prime\times_M\operatorname{Spec}D$. Tensoring the local finite free presentations preserves finite locally free source and target; etaleness of $a$ survives base change by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The three cartesian squares and all groupoid identities survive by the universal property of fibre products. We may therefore use the same hypotheses after any flat affine base change.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; flat base change paragraph; Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), flat case

proof.text: First suppose $C$ strictly henselian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and fix $p\prime\in M\prime$ above its closed point. Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-strict-local-reduced-orbit]. Its hypotheses are exactly the three cartesian squares and etaleness of $a$, together with the finite locally free affine presentations assumed here. With $J=\sqrt{\mathfrak m A}$ and $J\prime$ the radical ideal of the closed orbit $Z\prime=U\prime_{p\prime}$, it gives an isomorphism $A/J\to A\prime/J\prime$ and a bijection of those orbit points with $U_{\mathfrak m}$, with the same residue fields. In particular the inverse of this isomorphism, composed with the quotient $A\prime\to A\prime/J\prime$, is an $A$-algebra map $\bar\sigma:A\prime\to A/J$.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; claim, first part and reduced quotient identification

proof.text: By [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants], $A$ is integral over $C$. Since $C$ is henselian local, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair] makes $(A,\mathfrak m A)$ henselian. The map $A\to A\prime$ is etale, so [lem-sfb-henselian-pair-radical-etale-section] lifts $\bar\sigma$ to a retraction $\sigma:A\prime\to A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] to this retraction: $A\prime\simeq A\times A^{\prime\prime}$ over $A$. Denote by $W\simeq U$ the corresponding clopen subscheme of $U\prime$. The reduction of $\sigma$ is the specified inverse on $A/J$; hence $W$ contains every point of $Z\prime$, and its intersection with the inverse image of the closed point of $M$ is precisely $Z\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; claim, second part, henselian splitting

proof.text: The clopen $W$ is invariant. Indeed, $(s\prime)^{-1}W$ is finite over $W\simeq U$, so its ring is finite over $A$ and integral over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], hence integral over $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair] and [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-prime-connected] to see that every point of this source component has a specialization over the closed point of $M$: the closed set of specializations meeting the closed fibre is nonempty. Its specialized source belongs to $Z\prime$. Since invariant functions agree on the two endpoints of an arrow, the specialized target also lies over $p\prime$, hence belongs to $Z\prime\subset W$. Clopenness now forces the original target to lie in $W$. Inversion gives the reverse inclusion, so $(s\prime)^{-1}W=(t\prime)^{-1}W$. Their common clopen component maps isomorphically to $R$ by the source cartesian square and $W\simeq U$. The object and arrow isomorphisms respect all operations because $F$ does. Thus the whole groupoid splits as $(U,R)\amalg(U^{\prime\prime},R^{\prime\prime})$ over $(U,R)$. Taking the equalizer in these two product rings gives $C\prime\simeq C\times C^{\prime\prime}$. The point $p\prime$ belongs to the first factor: the nonempty orbit $Z\prime$ lies in $W$.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; end of claim; explicit specialization argument for invariance

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $C$ and $p\prime\mapsto p$. Take a separable closure of $\kappa(p)$ and the strict henselization $H$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. Use a small skeleton of the pointed etale algebras: their finite presentations and residue embeddings form a set. Thus $H$ is a small filtered colimit of pointed etale $C$-algebras $C_i$, and is strictly henselian. Each $C_i$ is flat over $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. The elementwise description [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] also gives the colimit of the underlying $C$-modules: a compatible family of linear maps acts on a representative at a stage, and equality at a later stage makes it well defined. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules] makes $C\to H$ flat. Choose $p\prime_H$ over $p\prime$ and the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}H$: the tensor product of their residue fields over $\kappa(p)$ is nonzero. Step 1 and steps 2--4 yield a section $U_H\to U\prime_H$ with clopen invariant image $W_H\simeq U_H$ through that orbit.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; strict henselization base change paragraph

proof.text: Descend this section algebraically. Its retraction is determined by the $A$-algebra map $A\prime\to A\otimes_C H$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] identifies $A\otimes_C H$ with the filtered colimit of the $A\otimes_C C_i$: a compatible cocone is exactly a fixed map from $A$ and a compatible cocone from the $C_i$. Since $A\prime$ is finitely presented over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization](1), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] factors this map through $A\otimes_C C_i$. Extending $C_i$-linearly gives a retraction $A\prime\otimes_C C_i\to A\otimes_C C_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] its image on spectra is clopen $W_i\simeq U_i$, described by an idempotent $\epsilon_i\in A\prime\otimes_C C_i$. At the limit its invariance is $(s\prime)^*\epsilon_i=(t\prime)^*\epsilon_i$ in $B\prime\otimes_C H$. The same universal property identifies $B\prime\otimes_C H$ with the filtered colimit of the $B\prime\otimes_C C_i$, and the images of $\epsilon_i$ in $A\prime\otimes_C H$ are the idempotent of the section over $H$, since the factorized retraction base changes to the given one. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](2), this equation holds at a later stage. Thus the groupoid splits there with first component $(U_i,R_i)$, and step 1 gives $C\prime\otimes_C C_i=C_i\times D_i$. The clopen factor $N_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i\subset M\prime\times_M\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ contains the image of $p\prime_H$. Its composite $N_i\to M\prime$ is etale (open immersion followed by base change of $\operatorname{Spec}C_i\to M$) and has $p\prime$ in its image. Its composite to $M$ is etale as well.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; descent of the decomposition, by finite presentation of the section and descent of one idempotent equation

proof.text: Choose these charts for all $p\prime\in M\prime$. Their coproduct $N\to M\prime$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], is surjective, and both $N\to M\prime$ and $N\to M$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] with $p:N\to M\prime$ surjective etale and $h:M\prime\to M$, whose composite $h\circ p:N\to M$ is etale. It follows that $M\prime\to M$ is etale. The comparison $d:U\prime\to U\times_M M\prime$ is consequently etale by base change and cancellation, since its composite to $U$ is the given etale map $a$.

source.place: Tag 0DT9 (lemma-etale), proof; conclusion of the descent paragraph and final paragraph

proof.text: To finish the omitted details, fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and an $\Omega$-point $(u,y)$ of $U\times_M M\prime$ with image $p\in M$. Choose the strict henselization $H$ at the separable closure of $\kappa(p)$ inside $\Omega$, with its map to $\Omega$. After this flat base change, apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-strict-local-reduced-orbit] to the point of $M\prime_H$ underlying $y$. It identifies its orbit with $U_{H,\mathfrak m_H}$ bijectively with identical residue fields. Each residue field of this latter fibre is algebraic over the separably closed residue field of $H$, by [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants] and [lem-a1-integral-residue-extension-algebraic]. Every finite subextension has a unique embedding into $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-finite-extension-unique-embedding](b). Those maps agree on composita, so their union is the unique embedding of the whole residue field. The orbit bijection and the identical residue fields therefore give exactly one $\Omega$-point above $(u,y)$; the compatibility with $y$ holds because the two embeddings of its algebraic residue field into $\Omega$ agree by the same finite-subextension argument. Thus $d$ is bijective on $\Omega$-points for every algebraically closed $\Omega$. Two points over any field become equal after passage to its algebraic closure and hence were equal already, so [def-weil-radicial-morphism] makes $d$ radicial. It is surjective on points by the same geometric-point existence. By [lem-weil-pbc-radicial-etale-open] it is an open immersion; a surjective open immersion is an isomorphism. Empty schemes make these checks vacuous. No constant-rank or Noetherian assumption was used.

Step 1: flat base change of invariants via flat-tensor-exact. Steps 2-3: the reduced-orbit isomorphism, then integral over henselian, the new radical-section lift and idempotent splitting. Step 4: invariance of W, using prime-connected for the specialization to the closed fibre, generization into the open W, and the source square for the arrow component. Both new nodes are true, self-contained and not restatements of the item. lem-sfb-groupoid-strict-local-reduced-orbit is the first part of the 0DT9 claim, checked by finiteness, closedness, bijection and CRT, and on the empty, identity and disjoint-copy cases. lem-sfb-henselian-pair-radical-etale-section is 09XJ plus 09XI (1)=>(2); the DAG has only the converse and the local rational-point version, so it is not a duplicate.
